The schematron's F5.1S/F5.1T sibling assertions -- the obligation's own remaining named gap -- are now also proven: when a non-isolated sc has a resolvable matching ec, canCopy/canDelete/canOverlap must be equivalent between the two (a "no" value on either side requires "no" on the other; "yes" and an absent attribute -- both meaning the same schema default -- are mutually compatible), and canReorder additionally allows sc's own "firstNo" value, which requires the matching ec's canReorder to be exactly "no". Two adjacent, honestly-documented notes, neither blocking this obligation's own rule_text: the pre-existing, separate per-segment sc/ec pairing check (xliff.inline.ec.unpaired) still does not look across segment boundaries within a unit, a distinct limitation discovered (not introduced or repaired) when the core isolated-attribute check was first built; and the schematron's F5.1S/F5.1T clause (a) -- exactly-one-matching-ec existence and document-order -- is not separately re-verified by the new attribute-matching check, since it only runs once _isolated_diagnostics has already proven a matching ec is present.
